input.prompt: Every time I change code a dev doc covers, I have to bump its Verified at by hand, and that often ends up as a separate commit. Can docs-check move a stale document's Verified at itself? And while you're there, CI runs every check and test suite one after another, which takes almost 5 minutes; can you split the tests into parallel shards?

required: --covering finds the doc that covers a file, and reports it current
--covering finds the doc that covers a folder holding the file, and reports it stale
--covering reports a path nothing covers, and counts docs with no Covers line
--covering searches the docs index by default and the given docs otherwise
--covering prints one line per covering doc as text
--covering exits 2 when the project has no docs index and none are given
--driven counts a covered change committed together with its doc, which the default treats as reviewed
--stamp moves a stale doc's Verified at to HEAD, so the doc and the code go in one commit
--stamp leaves a feature file alone, since its Verified at is the commit it was driven at
CI workflow covers generated output and release governance tests
CI and release workflows assert a clean worktree after tests
release workflow satisfies publication ordering and artifact invariants
rejects publication before release-note extraction
bounds npm registry propagation verification after publish
npm test runs every test:* suite, so a new suite cannot be left out of CI
CI's test shards run every suite npm test lists, each exactly once, including a suite added later
